name: What is the best foundation for a detached ADU on an LA lot?

mainEntity.name: What foundation type is usually best for a detached ADU in Los Angeles, and when does it change?
mainEntity.text: What foundation type is usually best for a detached ADU in Los Angeles, and when does it change?

acceptedAnswer.text: Foundation choice is one of the most important decisions in detached ADU construction because it affects cost, schedule, and structural performance. Flat, stable lots often work well with slab-on-grade construction, which can be efficient and straightforward. But once a lot has poor soils, slope, drainage challenges, or unusual loading conditions, the foundation may need to be engineered differently. That can mean deeper footings, piers, raised systems, or additional structural work. Homeowners should not assume one foundation type fits every property just because it worked on a neighboring lot. A proper site evaluation should consider soil report findings, grading, and how the unit will sit relative to the main house and existing drainage. The foundation decision often influences the whole project budget, so it should be made early rather than during plan check or after excavation begins.
acceptedAnswer.description: The best foundation depends on soil, slope, drainage, and structural loads. Slab-on-grade is often efficient on flat sites, while more complex lots may require deeper or engineered foundation systems to handle site conditions safely.
